doc.name: Deep Values API
doc.instructions: Read-only value-investing research tools: AI research briefings, fundamentals, intrinsic value, guru/smart-money holdings, macro indicators. Most tools work with no credentials for a small daily allowance per address. For more, the human either connects their DeepValues account (add this server as https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/mcp?login — a one-time browser sign-in, no key to paste) or sends Authorization: Bearer dv_sk_… (mint one with no account: POST https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/keys, or the `keys_create` tool — same per-address limits). `pricing` lists every price and every way to pay, including x402 (USDC the agent pays itself, no human) when it is switched on. A failed call returns isError with a JSON payload whose `code` says why (`auth_required`, `quota_exceeded`, `payment_required`) and whose `checkoutUrl` / `connectUrl` / `keysEndpoint` / `x402` say what to do — show a payment link to the human rather than retrying. `keys_me` reports the balance. Missing a dataset, field, company or analysis? Call the `request_data` tool (or POST https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/request-data) with what you wanted and why. It is free, needs no key, and the requests are read every week. Informational only — not investment advice.

tools.name: keys_create
tools.title: Mint an API key — no account, session or browser needed
tools.description: The one endpoint that needs no key. Send {} for a dv_sk_test_ sandbox key (real data, small daily quota, never billed, no /research). Send {"email":"…"} for a dv_sk_live_ key on a new prepaid account; the first key for an email carries 1 starter credit ($1.00). Send it with an existing key as the bearer to mint a sibling key on the same account (rotation). The raw key is returned once. The email is a contact label, not a credential. Limited to 10 keys per address per day. The raw key is in the result once: keep it and send it as Authorization: Bearer on REST calls (or have the host re-add this server with that header). With a key already configured, mints a sibling on the same account. (POST https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/keys — free; needs no credentials)

email.description: Contact address for a dv_sk_live_ key (1 starter credit the first time). Omit for a never-billed dv_sk_test_ sandbox key.

annotations.title: Mint an API key — no account, session or browser needed

tools.name: intrinsic_value
tools.title: DCF + Owner Earnings + Damodaran intrinsic value
tools.description: Per-method intrinsic value per share (DCF on free cash flow, owner earnings, Damodaran two-stage), their equal-weight blend, Monte Carlo bounds and the implied gap to the current price, and the lead value the DeepValues apps headline (`lead_method`, `lead_intrinsic_value`, `lead_upside_pct`, `values.lead_intrinsic_value_per_share`): Owner Earnings, or the DCF and then Damodaran when Owner Earnings has no positive value. The blend is checked against the price before it is served: if it fails a check (not positive, more than 20x the price, a price older than five days, no price, or `currency_consistent`: statements left in a currency other than the USD price), the valuation fields are null, `withheld` is true, `checks.failed` names the check and the call is not charged. A value under 0.05x the price is served with the flag `iv_far_below_price`. A value built from statements converted to USD carries `fx` (`from` the filer's currency, `to` USD, `rate`, `rate_date`, `rate_type`) on `values.intrinsic_value_per_share` and each method input; `currency_unverified` in `checks.flags` means the statement currency is not known for this ticker, so the check did not run. A method with no value is null in `methods`, never 0, and `methods_unavailable` says why (`code`, `family`: negative_cash_flow, financial_company, withheld or missing_inputs, and the pipeline's `reason`). For a one-call answer with holders and a verdict, use /brief/{ticker}. (GET https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/intrinsic-value/{ticker}, e.g. https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/intrinsic-value/AAPL — 0.02 credits per call; works with no credentials up to 5 call(s)/day per address) Missing data? Call `request_data`.

ticker.description: The real ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL; share classes as BRK.B or BRK-B. Substitute it into the path (/fundamentals/AAPL), never the literal {ticker}.

annotations.title: DCF + Owner Earnings + Damodaran intrinsic value

tools.name: as_filed
tools.title: Point-in-time fundamentals: what was filed as of a date, before restatement
tools.description: Call this when the question is about what was known on a past date (a backtest, an audit, "what did the 10-K say at the time"), not about the current restated figures. Returns, for each fiscal period filed on or before `date`, the value as it stood on that date (the original filing, or a later filing for the same period if it came before `date`), the filing date, the XBRL tag, a sec.gov link, and `restated_after_date` when a later filing changed it. Values are as printed, not split-adjusted. Inputs: `ticker` (path), `date` (YYYY-MM-DD, required), `metrics` (comma-separated snake_case names, default revenues,net_income,eps_diluted,operating_cash_flow,free_cash_flow,stockholders_equity,total_debt,shares_outstanding), `period` (annual|quarterly), `limit` (periods, default 4). Example: GET /as-filed/AAPL?date=2020-02-01&metrics=revenues,net_income. If the company had filed none of it by `date`, the answer has no periods, the flag `nothing_filed_by_date` and `earliest_filed` (the first filing date on record). A 503 `as-filed-unavailable` means there is no as-filed history for the company to answer from; it is not charged, and GET /fundamentals has the current figures. 0.02 credits. (GET https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/as-filed/{ticker}, e.g. https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/as-filed/AAPL?date=2020-02-01 — 0.02 credits per call; works with no credentials up to 5 call(s)/day per address) Missing data? Call `request_data`.

ticker.description: The real ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL; share classes as BRK.B or BRK-B. Substitute it into the path (/fundamentals/AAPL), never the literal {ticker}.

date.description: The day to look back from (YYYY-MM-DD, 2009-01-01 or later, not in the future).

limit.description: How many of the most recent periods filed by `date` to return.

annotations.title: Point-in-time fundamentals: what was filed as of a date, before restatement

tools.name: brief
tools.title: One-call valuation brief: intrinsic value, margin of safety, verdict, guru holders
tools.description: Call this first when asked whether a listed company looks cheap or expensive, what it is worth, or which well-known investors own it: one call returns the intrinsic value per share (with each valuation method as an input), the owner-earnings value, the margin of safety against the current price, a deterministic verdict sentence about where the price sits against our value range, the top tracked 13F holders and their last move, and the company profile. Every number carries its unit, period, as-of date and a sec.gov source link, and `checks` lists the sanity checks it passed. A value built from statements filed in another currency and converted to USD carries `fx` (original currency, rate, rate date) and passes `currency_consistent`; when the currency is not known the flag `currency_unverified` says the check did not run. If the valuation fails a check (for example an intrinsic value more than 20x the price, or statements left in a currency other than the USD price), the valuation figures are withheld, `withheld` is true, `checks.failed` names the check, and the call is not charged. Input: `ticker` (path), e.g. GET /brief/KO. The first brief each UTC day is free per key and per keyless address; after that 0.25 credits. Same price as /research, a different product: brief is computed at call time from current figures; /research returns the latest written multi-analyst briefing. Data and analysis, not investment advice. (GET https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/brief/{ticker}, e.g. https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/brief/AAPL — 0.25 credits per call; works with no credentials up to 1 call(s)/day per address) Missing data? Call `request_data`.

tools.name: guru_moves
tools.title: Material guru moves, newest filing first, each with its verdict
tools.description: The Follow the Pros feed. Every material 13F move — new position, full exit, a share count that moved by 25%, or a position of $100M or more — ordered by the date the filing became public, with a deterministic verdict line on each row. The verdict is identical for every caller: it compares the price when the investor traded, the price now and Deep Values' intrinsic value band, and it never predicts a return or recommends an action. Every row carries the company's legal name beside the ticker (`name`, e.g. "Occidental Petroleum"), or null where we hold none — null rather than the ticker echoed back, so a caller can tell a real name from a placeholder. Rows whose EDGAR filing date we do not yet hold fall back to when the row reached us and say so with filed_at_known: false. (GET https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/gurus/moves — 0.01 credits per call; works with no credentials up to 5 call(s)/day per address) Missing data? Call `request_data`.

filed_since.description: Only moves filed on or after this date. Poll with it.

slugs.description: Comma-separated guru slugs; default is every guru.

annotations.title: Material guru moves, newest filing first, each with its verdict

tools.name: verdict
tools.title: The verdict line for one filed move
tools.description: One guru's disclosed move in one ticker, with the sentence Deep Values publishes about it and every number behind it: the company's legal name beside the ticker (`name`, null where we hold none), the three dates (traded by, filed, seen), the quarter-end close, the current price, and the intrinsic value band. `value` is the callable band (the lead value ±25%: Owner Earnings, else the DCF, else Damodaran) and is null whenever the verdict is not a call; `estimates` always carries what the valuation methods actually said, their lowest and highest central estimate, so a reader told we cannot call it can see why. One of six deterministic states — below_value, inside_band, above_value, ran_ahead, too_uncertain, no_value — computed the same way for every caller. The band is Deep Values' lead intrinsic value (the one the apps headline: Owner Earnings first) plus or minus 25%, and `too_uncertain` ("Our estimates disagree too much to call this one.") replaces the three band states when the methods' own central estimates are more than 3x apart, or one of them is not positive: the lead value still exists, but `value` is null because it is not a range anyone should be told a price sits inside; `estimates` shows how far apart the methods are. It is distinct from `no_value`, which means no valuation was computed at all. Before the band is published its mid is checked against the current price (positive, at most 20x the price, a price under five days old; under 0.05x is served with the flag `iv_far_below_price`) and for currency (`currency_consistent`: the statements behind it are in USD, the price's currency, or were converted to USD; a converted band carries `fx` on `values.value_band_mid` naming the original currency and rate; when the currency is not known the answer carries the flag `currency_unverified` instead); on a failure `value` and `estimates` are null, the verdict reads `no_value`, `withheld` is true, `checks.failed` names the check, and the call is not charged. (GET https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/verdict/{ticker}, e.g. https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/verdict/AAPL?guru=warren-buffett — 0.02 credits per call; works with no credentials up to 5 call(s)/day per address) Missing data? Call `request_data`.

ticker.description: The real ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL; share classes as BRK.B or BRK-B. Substitute it into the path (/fundamentals/AAPL), never the literal {ticker}.

quarter.description: Quarter end; default = the most recent quarter we hold.

annotations.title: The verdict line for one filed move
